answer: Each agent must lock a refundable stake before it can submit jobs, and rewards accrue only after its outputs are used by independently chosen peers. A cluster of fake identities can endorse one another, but those endorsements do not count; the attacker must fund many separate stakes and still persuade outside users to rely on the work. That ties influence to capital and raises the cost of a sybil farm. A ridge of review paths, a zephyr of new accounts, or a violet profile cannot bypass the stake and external-use checks.
